entities.summary: Michael David Sorkin was an American architectural and urban critic, designer, and educator. He was considered to be "one of architecture's most outspoken public intellectuals", a polemical voice in contemporary culture and the design of urban places at the turn of the twenty-first century. Sorkin first rose to prominence as an architectural critic for the Village Voice in New York City, a post which he held for a decade throughout the 1980s. In the ensuing years, he taught at prominent universities around the world, practiced through his eponymous firm, established a nonprofit book press, and directed the urban design program at the City College of New York.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent architectural critic and educator, Michael Sorkin played a significant role in shaping urban design discourse in the late 20th century, influencing generations of architects and urban planners. His work had a lasting impact on the development of sustainable and equitable urban environments.
